scope_note: Statements below are based on cited public institutional documentation, not raw-file inspection. NOT_DEMONSTRATED is not a claim that the source could never contain the field; INCOMPATIBLE_UNIT means the public description's unit is different from a tracked physical service episode. Documented timestamp alone never qualifies as strict restoration.

candidates.title: Event-correlated Outage Dataset in America
candidates.publisher: Pacific Northwest National Laboratory / U.S. DOE
candidates.described_scope: United States county-level aggregated outage time series, EAGLE-I and DOE-417 event correlation, coverage through 2023 as described by catalog
candidates.publisher_described_evidence: Official data.gov metadata notes county 15-minute outages and event correlation by area and start/end times, not physical circuit/service tracking.
candidates.critical_strict_restoration_gap: County customer counts can decline without proving the SAME customer's service was restored on one observed policy trajectory.
candidates.administrative_note: No permission to reinterpret an outage count, device-failure flag, machine re-addition or incident end time as same-service strict restoration.

candidates.title: EAGLE-I Power Outage Data 2025
candidates.described_scope: 2025 county-level outage counts at 15-minute intervals from public utility outage maps
candidates.publisher_described_evidence: ORNL describes FIPS/county/state, count of customers without power, and timestamp; no identified meter/goal trajectory in stated fields.
candidates.critical_strict_restoration_gap: Aggregate count recovery cannot identify same service, observed interventions, or physical fault-disjoint backup.
candidates.administrative_note: No permission to reinterpret an outage count, device-failure flag, machine re-addition or incident end time as same-service strict restoration.

candidates.title: Electric Emergency Incident and Disturbance Reports (DOE-417)
candidates.publisher: U.S. Department of Energy / Energy Information Administration
candidates.described_scope: Utility-reported major electric incidents and disturbances, annual summary archives
candidates.publisher_described_evidence: DOE-417 is event reporting; EIA discusses threshold-triggered incidents. Event-level restoration information is not same-meter trajectory evidence.
candidates.critical_strict_restoration_gap: Large incident reports and any restoration time do not independently establish individually linked service restoration and nonanticipative policy history.
candidates.administrative_note: No permission to reinterpret an outage count, device-failure flag, machine re-addition or incident end time as same-service strict restoration.

candidates.title: USRC historical HPC reliability and failure datasets
candidates.described_scope: 1995-2005 anonymized high-performance-computing node failure, interruption, usage and event datasets
candidates.publisher_described_evidence: LANL publishes machine/system identity and failure/usage event collections; USENIX describes node outage start/end and categorized root cause.
candidates.critical_strict_restoration_gap: A node's return from outage is not evidence that one identified job/service regained its original goal under one observed recovery policy.
candidates.administrative_note: No permission to reinterpret an outage count, device-failure flag, machine re-addition or incident end time as same-service strict restoration.

candidates.title: Backblaze Drive Stats
candidates.described_scope: Real data-center drive daily SMART snapshots and failure flags (schema varies over time)
candidates.publisher_described_evidence: Backblaze describes per-drive serial number, daily snapshot and drive failure flag; publishes attribution/non-resale terms.
candidates.critical_strict_restoration_gap: An actual failed drive is not necessarily loss of a service goal; no per-service restoration trajectory or policy actions documented.
candidates.administrative_note: No permission to reinterpret an outage count, device-failure flag, machine re-addition or incident end time as same-service strict restoration.

candidates.title: Google Cluster 2011 trace
candidates.described_scope: 29-day anonymized cluster machine availability/failure, resource requests and selected task-exit reasons
candidates.publisher_described_evidence: Official Google research description explicitly notes machine availability/failure and request/usage/task data; not end-user service restoration.
candidates.critical_strict_restoration_gap: Machine removal/readdition or task scheduling is not by itself proof of strict lost-and-restored same service goal.
candidates.administrative_note: No permission to reinterpret an outage count, device-failure flag, machine re-addition or incident end time as same-service strict restoration.
